column5: C_p: the completion of an algebraic closure of Q_p for the unique extension of the p-adic absolute value, normalised by |p| = 1/p. column5: For an odd prime d and an integer a: (a/d) = 0 if d | a, 1 if a is a nonzero square mod d, -1 otherwise. Used as chi_K(p) = (p/d) for a prime d = 7 mod 8: it is 1, -1, 0 as p splits, is inert, ramifies in Q(sqrt(-d)).
An integer a prime to m is a quadratic residue mod m if x^2 = a (mod m) is solvable.

For an odd prime p and an integer a: a^((p-1)/2) = (a/p) (mod p). Used in the form: in a ring of characteristic p (p odd, p not dividing d), (sqrt(-d))^(p^n) = chi_K(p)^n sqrt(-d), with chi_K(p) = (p/d) = (-d/p) for d = 3 mod 4.
For distinct odd primes p, q: (p/q)(q/p) = (-1)^((p-1)(q-1)/4); with the supplements for -1 and 2.
v_p(n!) = sum_{i>=1} floor(n/p^i) = (n - s_p(n))/(p-1), where s_p(n) is the sum of the base-p digits of n. Consequence used: n/(p-1) - K <= v_p(n!) <= n/(p-1) when n < p^K.

Then the extension to O_L of the different of K2 divides the relative different of L over K1 (in fact equals it, and O_L = O_K1 O_K2). If a prime ideal P of O_L has p in P^2 for the rational prime p below it (ramification index > 1), then P divides the different of L over Q.
